conn.hosted: Prefer the hosted surface unless you are the only person using this Khepri. Its keys are per person and revocable without a restart.
conn.intro: Let an agent you already use — Claude Code, Codex, Hermes — read your goals, log check-ins, and ask your coach. Each connection gets its own key, so you can turn one off without touching the others.
conn.issued.desc: Copy this now. It is not stored, so it cannot be shown again — if you lose it, revoke this connection and make another.
conn.issued.prompt.note: Or paste this into the agent itself and let it do the setup. It sends the key to whichever model that agent runs on, so use it with an agent you would trust with your coaching data — and revoke the key here if you change your mind.
conn.list.desc: Every one of these can read and write your coaching data. Revoke anything you do not recognise.

conn.name: Name this connection

conn.provider.note.anthropic: Claude on your own Anthropic account. Billed to that account.
conn.provider.note.hermes: Your own Hermes instance — tailnet, LAN, or public. URL and key stay on this account.
conn.provider.note.nvidia: Free models, and what Khepri's own free tier already runs on.
conn.provider.note.openai: Needs no new code: openaicompat speaks OpenAI's dialect already.
conn.provider.note.openrouter: One key, most models — including Claude and GPT. The simplest choice.
conn.revoke.desc: That agent stops being able to read or change anything straight away. The key cannot be turned back on; you would connect the agent again with a new one.
conn.revoke.title: Revoke %[1]s?
conn.setup.safe.claude: If that file lives in a git repository, use this version instead and keep the key in your environment — .mcp.json is committed more often than people expect.

conn.tg.desc: Message your coach from your phone. Same memory, same goals, same conversation — what you ask in Telegram carries on in the web chat, and the other way round.

land.bmi.read.normal: {n} sits inside the range everyone chases, and it still tells you nothing about whether you can carry a pack for ninety minutes. Khepri tracks that instead.
land.bmi.read.obese: At {n} the number is loud, and it is still one weak signal. The first thing Khepri would change is not your weight but how many sessions in a row you finish.
land.bmi.read.over: The index says {n} and cannot tell muscle from anything else. Khepri watches waist, resting heart rate, and whether your lifts still climb while you eat less — those three disagree with BMI often enough to be the ones worth measuring.
land.bmi.read.under: At {h}cm and {w}kg the index reads {n}, which usually means eating is the training. Khepri would put food and sleep ahead of any programme for the first month.

land.feat.1.body: Every goal, session, check-in, and offhand remark stays. Khepri reads back across months, not across the last ten messages, so the injury you mentioned in March still shapes the plan in September.
land.feat.1.name: Persistent memory
land.feat.2.body: Before it answers, Khepri assembles what it knows: active goals, this week's training, your documents, your calendar, how you have been sleeping. Advice arrives already fitted to your life.
land.feat.2.name: Context-aware coaching

land.hero.badge: An operating system for personal growth
land.hero.free: Free while you find out whether it sticks. No card.
land.hero.h1a: Most AI forgets you by Tuesday.
land.hero.h1b: Khepri has been keeping notes since March.
land.hero.lede: One coach with one memory — on the web, in Telegram, and inside any tool that speaks MCP. It holds your goals, your training, the photos you send, your documents, and every check-in you have ever written.
land.how.1.body: In your own words, badly. Khepri turns it into an objective, a horizon, and a first week.
land.how.1.name: Say where you are going
land.how.2.body: Your equipment, your limits, your calendar, your documents. The plan is assembled from what is true about you, not from a template.
land.how.2.name: It builds the context
land.how.3.body: Check in from whichever app is in your hand. A sentence is enough. Khepri is keeping the ledger.
land.how.3.name: You just live
land.how.4.body: When the pattern shifts — sleep, pain, a missed block — Khepri moves before you fall off, and tells you what it saw.

land.iphone.1.body: The weight and reps are asked before the workout moves on, prefilled from your last set or last time. Records and estimated maxes follow on their own.
land.iphone.1.title: Every set, weighed
land.iphone.2.body: Sleep stages, HRV, resting heart rate, steps, VO2 max and workouts flow in; finished workouts flow back out.
land.iphone.2.title: Apple Health, both ways
land.iphone.3.body: A Live Activity counts your rest down and tells you what is next.
land.iphone.3.title: Rest on the Lock Screen
land.iphone.4.body: Sleep, cardio, eating, lifting and patterns, the same numbers as the web.
land.iphone.4.title: Stats in your pocket
land.iphone.body: The iPhone app is the same Khepri, with the parts a phone is for: a workout that asks for the weight before every set, Apple Health synced in the background, and My Day on the Today tab.
land.iphone.title: The gym is where the numbers happen.

land.surf.title: Four apps. One conversation. Nothing repeated back.
land.surf.wa.1: You told me on Monday that five hours of sleep is your line. You have hit it four nights this week. Before we add load, that is the thing worth fixing.
land.surf.web.1: Back is fine but I only slept five hours. Do I still squat today?
land.surf.web.2: No. You have squatted heavy on under six hours twice this year and both times the following week went missing. Do the Wednesday session today — dumbbell work and the carry — and move the squat to Thursday.

land.thread.2.body: Then we build around the back first. Six weeks of hinge tolerance before anything gets heavy.
land.thread.4.body: Fourth session in a row with no pain. That is the signal I was waiting for — moving you into the loading block.
land.thread.5.body: Gerês is five weeks out. Your longest carry so far is 40 minutes. We should get that to 90.
land.tools.body: Anything can compute a BMI. The work is knowing what it is worth — and what to do on Tuesday.
land.tools.title: Numbers are the easy part.
land.vision.1.body: The horizon plans are written against, not the session in front of you.
land.vision.2.body: Web and Telegram — and one memory behind both.
land.vision.3.body: Times you re-explain your injury, your equipment, or what you are training for.
land.vision.body: A good coach is not smarter than the internet. A good coach knows that you always quit in week five, that you lie about sleep, and that the last time you tried this you injured yourself doing something you were told not to do. That knowledge takes months to build and it is the entire product. Khepri is not trying to be a better chatbot — it is trying to be the thing that has been paying attention.
land.vision.quote: The useful thing was never the answer. It was that somebody had been watching long enough to notice the pattern.

tg.help:
Ask me anything you would ask in the web app — how a goal is going, what your week looked like, whether to train today.

This is the same conversation as the web chat. Ask here, and the answer is there too.

Before I write anything down — a check-in, a goal — I will show you what I am about to do and wait for a yes.

/help — this message
/stats — how things are going (add week, month or year)
/unlink — disconnect this chat from your account
tg.linked: Linked to %[1]s. Message me whenever — I have the same memory and goals as the web app.
tg.nocredit: I cannot reach a model right now — the service is out of credit. Try again in a moment.

You are linked to %[1]s. Ask me anything you would ask in the web app — I have the same memory, goals and check-ins.

Send /help to see what I can do.
